profile.reading:
Per NTT's own Global Data Centers facility page, this building, NTT Chicago CH2, is located at 275 Pierce Rd, Itasca, IL 60143, directly adjacent to NTT's original CH1 building on the same Itasca, DuPage County campus. The operator publishes 126,000 square feet of data floor space and 36 megawatts of critical IT load for this specific building, describing it in its own newsroom materials as a newer addition to the campus; no formal certifications or specific opening year are stated on the page. Together, CH1 and CH2 account for 72 of the roughly 200-plus megawatts NTT describes for its full Chicago-area campus, implying substantial additional capacity in further campus buildings.

Illinois's data center tax incentive program has become a flashpoint for state energy policy. Governor JB Pritzker announced on June 5, 2026 a temporary suspension of new awards under the state's Data Center Investment Program, citing grid strain; ComEd's CEO stated the program had added roughly $12 a month to the average residential bill over the prior four years. ComEd's northern Illinois service territory is separately projected to face capacity shortfalls beginning around 2029 as data center demand grows, a dynamic pushing new development toward Chicago's southern suburbs where power is more readily available, according to legal-industry analysis of ComEd's planning filings.

NTT's US Global Data Centers footprint spans seven named campuses in total: Ashburn, Virginia at 224 megawatts; Chicago, Illinois at more than 200 megawatts; Dallas, Texas at 160 megawatts; Hillsboro, Oregon at 126 megawatts; Phoenix, Arizona at 240 megawatts; and a combined Sacramento/Santa Clara, California figure of 68 megawatts, totaling roughly 1,118 megawatts or more of disclosed US capacity, per the operator's own locations page. The US business operates under the NTT DATA Global Data Centers Americas name, the successor brand to RagingWire Data Centers, now under Japan's NTT DATA Group and parent Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corporation, a Tokyo Stock Exchange-listed company not subject to SEC 10-K filing requirements.

NTT operates a global data center business, NTT Global Data Centers, under NTT DATA, Inc. The operators own about us page, fetched this session, states NTT DATA is a top 10 global IT services provider with about 30 billion dollars in annual revenue, operations across 33 countries, and about 3 billion dollars in annual research and development investment, headquartered at the Toyosu Center Building, 3-3-3 Toyosu, Koto-ku, Tokyo 135-6033, Japan, though these figures describe the wider NTT DATA organization rather than the data center division specifically, and no data center division formation or acquisition date was found on the pages fetched this session. A previously confirmed, specific data center acquisition remains NTT Communications purchase of an 86.7 percent stake in e-shelter, described as Germany top data center operator, completed around June 23, 2015, though that acquisition is not directly connected to this United States facility. This session reached the operators own services.global.ntt data center locations pages directly and successfully. An earlier sessions attempts to reach the ragingwire.com domain had failed and found no corresponding Wikipedia article, a negative finding this session did not need to repeat. reading.body:
NTT Chicago CH2 is a 36-megawatt building occupying 126,000 square feet at 275 Pierce Rd in Itasca, Illinois, part of NTT's multi-building Chicago-area campus. NTT publishes a total capacity of more than 200 megawatts across the full Chicago campus, of which CH1 and CH2 together account for 72 megawatts, implying at least two additional active buildings with published specifications on the same site. At the commonly observed density of 40 kilowatts per rack for AI training workloads, this single building's 36 megawatts of IT load is roughly equivalent to 900 racks. No formal certifications are published for this building.

Illinois is the seventh-largest published data center capacity state in the nation by total disclosed megawattage. This facility ranks seventh by published megawatts among all facilities in Illinois and represents roughly 15 percent of the 236 megawatts of published capacity in the state across six facilities with disclosed figures. Of 44 mapped data center facilities in Illinois, only six operators publish power specifications, indicating most capacity figures remain proprietary.

The political and grid environment around this campus has tightened. On June 5, 2026, Illinois Governor JB Pritzker suspended new awards under the state's Data Center Investment Program, citing grid strain, after the program had added roughly twelve dollars monthly to average residential bills over the prior four years. ComEd's northern Illinois service territory is projected to face capacity shortfalls beginning around 2029 as data center demand grows, a dynamic documented in legal analysis of ComEd's planning filings to push new development toward Chicago's southern suburbs where power is more readily available, a constraint that may limit expansion potential for northern sites like this Itasca location.
